notes.short: Holiness does not pass by touch; uncleanness does
notes.about: Haggai puts two cases to the priests. Holy meat carried in a garment's fold does not hallow the food it touches, but one defiled by a corpse defiles what he touches. He applies it: “So it is with this people.” Their holy things could not hallow them, but their uncleanness defiled all they did.

figure.name: Simile
figure.words: So it is with this people and this nation before Me
figure.means: the people before God: the holy things they had could not make them or their work holy, but their own uncleanness defiled all their work and offerings

notes.evidence: C. F. Keil (Keil and Delitzsch) says the people resemble both the man carrying holy flesh and the one defiled by a corpse. A. R. Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) says the first case shows a sacrifice cannot hallow the disobedient. Adam Clarke says their neglect of the temple made them unclean, as if by touching a dead body. Matthew Henry says the laws of clean and unclean illustrate it.
notes.limit: One writer applies it also to those now building the temple with unholy hearts, not only to the years of neglect before.

cites.quote: The prophet now applies these provisions of the law to the ethical relation in which the people stood to Jehovah. ... The nation, in its attitude towards the Lord, resembles, on the one hand, a man who carries holy flesh in the lappet of his garment, and on the other hand, a man who has become unclean through touching a corpse.

cites.quote: This is cited to illustrate the principle, that a sacrifice, holy, as enveloping divine things (just as the "skirt" is "holy" which envelops "holy" flesh), cannot by its inherent or opus operatum efficacy make holy a person whose disobedience, as that of the Jew while neglecting God's house, made him unholy.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: As an unclean man communicates his uncleanness to every thing he touches, so are ye unclean; and whatever ye have hitherto done is polluted in the sight of God. For your neglect of my temple has made you unclean, as if you had contracted legal pollution by touching a dead body.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: God sees there are many among them that spoil this good work, by going about it with unsanctified hearts and hands ... This matter is here illustrated by the established rules of the ceremonial law ... They have been thus before God; they thought their offering sacrifices on the altar would sanctify them, and excuse their neglect to build the temple
